cards.text: The prophet Zephaniah has been bringing the LORD's words (Zephaniah 1:1), and the last ones were heavy: the LORD will pour out His burning anger on nations and kingdoms, and all the earth will be consumed by the fire of His jealousy (Zephaniah 3:8). Then the LORD keeps going, friend, and the very next words out of His mouth are "For then."

cards.question: For then, the LORD says, He'll restore something to the peoples so all may call upon His name. What does He restore?

cards.text: All of them, serving the LORD "shoulder to shoulder." I spent YEARS shoulder to shoulder with dead batteries in a junk drawer, and all we ever did was argue about who had the most charge left.

cards.question: The LORD says His scattered worshipers are too far away, beyond the rivers of Cush, to ever bring Him an offering.

cards.text: Now the LORD turns to His own people and all the wrongs they've done against Him. Friend, if that were me, I'd be sweating right through my apron.

cards.question: On that day, the LORD says His people will still be put to shame for every wrong they did against Him.
The LORD will remove from among His people those who rejoice in their ___. And never again will they be haughty on His holy mountain.

cards.text: Pride is OUT on His holy mountain. I used to be proud of my crisp edges, right up until I spent years under a pile of takeout menus in the back of a drawer.

cards.question: With the proud removed, who does the LORD say He'll leave within His people?
That meek and humble people will ___ in the name of the LORD.

cards.text: The remnant of Israel won't do wrong or speak lies, and no deceitful tongue will be found in their mouths. Not even "I'm five minutes away" when you haven't found your keys yet.

cards.question: With no one to make them tremble, what will the remnant of Israel do?

cards.text: Then comes a call, and it is LOUD: sing for joy, shout aloud, be glad and rejoice with all your heart, Daughter of Jerusalem! That's me when a batch comes out of the oven perfect, except I live alone, so mostly I'm just yelling at a cookie.

cards.question: Why all the joy? The call says the LORD has taken something away from His people. What is it?
The call says Israel's King, the LORD, is among His people, and they will no longer fear any harm.

cards.text: On that day, they'll say to Jerusalem: "Do not fear, O Zion; do not let your hands fall limp." That's the exact opposite of your boss texting "got a minute?" and every bone in your body quitting at once.

cards.question: What reason do they give Zion not to fear?

answers.text: The LORD is among you and mighty to save
Your walls are rebuilt and standing strong
Your army is gathered and ready for battle

cards.text: And it gets better, friend. He will rejoice over you with gladness, and He will quiet you with His love.

cards.question: The LORD will rejoice over His people with ___.

cards.text: I sing over my cookies, and honestly, the cookies have asked me to stop. But the LORD rejoicing over His people with singing is a song I'd shut down every oven to hear.

cards.question: The LORD speaks again. Who does He say He'll gather, so they will no longer suffer reproach?

answers.text: Those who grieve over the appointed feasts
Those who rejoice in their pride
Those who rule over the nations

cards.text: Then the LORD says, "Behold, at that time, I will deal with all who afflict you." ALL of them, friend. Nobody slips out the back door.

cards.question: At that time, the LORD will save the ___ and gather the ___.
The LORD says the disgraced will stay hidden in their shame, far from the rest of the earth.
When the LORD restores His people's captives before their very eyes, among whom will He give them fame and praise?

answers.text: All the peoples of the earth

cards.text: "At that time I will bring you in; yes, at that time I will gather you." Friend, after years in the back of a junk drawer, I can tell you there are no sweeter words than "I will bring you in."

findings.problem: Stop 2, card 14 quotes "I will bring you in.", which isn't the exact BSB wording.

rule.text: Quotes: Quotation marks around Bible words mean the exact BSB wording, punctuation included.

findings.problem: This story card tells nothing new from the passage. It repeats Zephaniah 3:11 (pride removed from His holy mountain), which cards 5 to 7 already covered, and exists only to carry a joke. Cards 9 and 10 move straight on to 3:12.

rule.text: Every story card moves the baker forward through the passage.

findings.problem: The joke adds something new to the Millers' kitchen backstory: that Papa Dorin was proud of his crisp edges. "Right up until" also ties that pride to his years in the drawer. The backstory says he went into the drawer because he was worn down, not because of pride.

rule.text: His backstory, family, bakery and mission are the Dorinverse story in this file. He can talk about them freely, but never adds anything new to them. His jokes can make up small moments and habits around his bakery.

findings.problem: Zephaniah 3:15 says "He has turned back your enemy." No story card tells this and no choice card asks it, so the baker never hears that part of why the call to rejoice is made.

rule.text: When the baker leaves Prep, they understand the whole passage without missing an important detail.

findings.problem: "What reason do they give Zion not to fear?" relies on "they" from card 4, which is no longer on screen. It also puts "will say" into the present tense ("give"). The question should carry its own context, for example "On that day, what reason will Zion be given not to fear?"

rule.text: Always give context in the question. The story card before it isn't on screen anymore, so the question says who and what. Never "him," "that" or "it" pointing back to a card the baker can't see.

findings.problem: Card 6 tells the first two lines of 3:17. The blank then asks the baker to supply the next line's wording: singing, trumpets or dancing. Nothing told so far lets a baker reason to "singing" over the other two. It is a guess at wording, not meaning.

rule.text: Never ask the baker to guess the next words of a line.

findings.problem: This story card tells nothing new from the passage. It repeats the answer to card 7 (the LORD rejoicing with singing, 3:17) and exists only to carry a joke.

rule.text: Every story card moves the baker forward through the passage.

findings.problem: Zephaniah 3:18 says "I will gather those among you who grieve over the appointed feasts, so that you will no longer suffer reproach." The question changes "you" (the people) to "they" (the gathered ones). That decides how the gathering and the end of reproach connect, which the text leaves open.

rule.text: Leave open what the text leaves open: who is being spoken to, why, or how two things connect.

findings.problem: This story card has three sentences: the quote, "ALL of them, friend." and "Nobody slips out the back door."

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

findings.problem: Card 13 asks about the end of 3:20 (fame and praise among all the peoples when the captives are restored). Card 14 then goes back to tell the start of 3:20 ("At that time I will bring you in..."). The walkthrough ends by stepping backward instead of following the passage's order.

rule.text: Every passage has a flow: the events of a story, the lines of a song, the steps of a letter's argument, the movement of a prophet's message. Papa Dorin moves the baker along that flow.
